title: Migrating to sim_events()
text: sim_model() call three kinds possible inputs: sim_covariate(): baseline covariate generator. Takes N , optionally, covariate defined earlier call (matched argument name). sim_process(): "censoring", "terminal", "transient" (fires limit times, default Inf) process, Weibull eta/nu parameters given cumulative baseline hazard curve (cumhaz). sim_effect(): -> edge Cox-type coef, covariate process name process name. sim_events()’s intervene argument replaces sim.generic()’s alpha.intervention/baseline.intervention pair single named list: give process name scale eta, covariate name fix constant. sim_effect()’s doesn’t name single covariate process. string parsed evaluated R expression, every covariate/process value plus current time t, event times T_<proc>.<k> (time proc’s k-th event, 0 hasn’t happened yet) last_time(proc). Covers thresholds, interactions, nonlinear transforms inline, effects depending process’s full occurrence history, just current count, without separate sim_derived() covariate. example, effect fires process’s 3rd occurrence, 1st 2nd: deaths happen right 3rd relapse, . T_<proc>.<k> last_time() give access timing, just counts. T_<proc>.<k> time proc’s k-th event, 0 hasn’t happened yet. Effects time since event therefore take form proc * f(t - T_proc.k): multiplying event count switches effect event happened, whatever f . death hazard spikes right operation fades: Without operation *, -yet-operated exp(-(t - 0)) = exp(-t), spike time 0 never happened. risk instead builds operation, use operation * (t - T_operation.1). death hazard drops one time unit right checkup: last_time(proc) -Inf proc’s first occurrence, t - last_time(proc) < 1 needs NA handling.

what: Simulating New Data from a Fitted Model
title: Getting Started with simevent
text: Besides simulating user-specified parameters, simevent can simulate new data model already fitted observed data. simEventCox() Cox proportional hazards models, simEventObj() model equipped predict2 method. Say observed data: Fit Cox models events interest, pass fitted models simEventCox(): New baseline covariates simulated resampling rows old_vars. simEventObj() works fitted model, long equip predict2() method returning times cumulative hazard new covariate values. example, Cox model:
code: set.seed(373) beta <- matrix(c(0.5, -1, -0.5, 0.5, 0, 0.5), ncol = 3, nrow = 2) data <- simCRdata(N = 1000, beta = beta) cox1 <- coxph(Surv(Time, Delta == 1) ~ L0 + A0, data = data) cox2 <- coxph(Surv(Time, Delta == 2) ~ L0 + A0, data = data)  cox_fits <- list("Process 1" = cox1, "Process 2" = cox2) old_vars <- data[, c(4, 5)] new_data <- simEventCox(100, cox_fits, old_vars = old_vars) head(new_data) #> Key: <ID> #>       ID      Time Delta        L0    A0 Process 1 Process 2 #>    <int>     <num> <num>     <num> <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:     1 0.4931728     1 0.5363954     0         0         1 #> 2:     1 4.0046486     0 0.5363954     0         1         1 #> 3:     2 0.6828662     1 0.3144497     0         0         1 #> 4:     2 9.8772172     0 0.3144497     0         1         1 #> 5:     3 0.8909987     1 0.9335247     1         0         1 #> 6:     3 4.2916262     0 0.9335247     1         1         1 cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(Time, Delta == 1) ~ L0 + A0, data = data)  predict2 <- function(obj, ...) UseMethod("predict2") predict2.coxph <- function(obj, sim_data, ...) {   preds <- survfit(obj, newdata = sim_data)   # preds$cumhaz is a times x individuals matrix; reshape to individuals x times x events   chf <- array(t(preds$cumhaz), dim = c(nrow(sim_data), length(preds$time), 1))   list(time = preds$time, chf = chf) }  old_vars <- data[, c("L0", "A0")] new_data <- simEventObj(100, cox_fit, old_vars = old_vars) head(new_data) #> Key: <ID> #>       ID      Time Delta          L0    A0    N0 #>    <int>     <num> <num>       <num> <num> <num> #> 1:     1       Inf     0 0.926276597     0     0 #> 2:     2       Inf     0 0.730683018     0     0 #> 3:     3 13.181177     1 0.057044588     0     1 #> 4:     4  8.531944     1 0.006538616     1     1 #> 5:     5  1.371236     1 0.921506565     1     1 #> 6:     6  4.866903     1 0.240172203     0     1

Every simulated dataset includes two baseline covariates, L0 (baseline covariate, Uniform(0,1) default) A0 (baseline treatment indicator, Bernoulli(0.5) default), followed covariates supplied via add_cov. L0/A0 just first two entries covariate-generation list: generator may depend covariate defined earlier list name (e.g. default A0 generator takes L0 argument), add_cov can supply "L0"/"A0" entries, later covariates conditional earlier ones (see add_cov ).

Formula terms may transform interact covariates (e.g. (age^2), L0:A0). process uses fit's cumulative baseline hazard sim_process() cumhaz, simulated follow-ends last time data. formula term naming another process (e.g. relapse ~ L0 + relapse) becomes sim_effect() process. coefficient valid fit treated time-varying (e.g. using interval_format_data()).

code: library(survival)  # Some "observed" data, from a 3-cause competing-risks sim_model(): set.seed(1405) observed_model <- sim_model(   L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) runif(N)),   A0 = sim_covariate(function(N, L0) rbinom(N, 1, plogis(-0.5 + L0))),   censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),   cause1 = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),   cause2 = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),   effects = list(     sim_effect("L0", "censoring", 0.5),     sim_effect("A0", "censoring", -1),     sim_effect("L0", "cause1", -0.5),     sim_effect("A0", "cause1", 0.5),     sim_effect("A0", "cause2", 0.5)   ) ) observed_data <- sim_events(observed_model, n = 1000)  # Refit each process from that "observed" data, then rebuild a sim_model() # from the fits, as if observed_data came from an outside source and # observed_model were unknown: fits <- list(   censoring = coxph(     Surv(time, event == "censoring") ~ L0 + A0,     data = observed_data   ),   cause1 = coxph(Surv(time, event == "cause1") ~ L0 + A0, data = observed_data),   cause2 = coxph(Surv(time, event == "cause2") ~ L0 + A0, data = observed_data) ) types <- c(censoring = "censoring", cause1 = "terminal", cause2 = "terminal")  model <- sim_model_from_fits(fits, observed_data, types) new_data <- sim_events(model, n = 1000) head(new_data) #> Key: <id> #>       id     time     event        L0    A0 #>    <int>    <num>    <fctr>     <num> <num> #> 1:     1 1.512868    cause2 0.9559121     1 #> 2:     2 2.208823    cause2 0.9885974     0 #> 3:     3 2.047464    cause2 0.4766994     1 #> 4:     4 1.677063 censoring 0.1054270     0 #> 5:     5 1.145823    cause1 0.5620987     0 #> 6:     6 4.629326    cause1 0.1166055     1  # Event-type distribution should be comparable between the observed and # newly simulated data (a few simulated individuals reach the end of the # observed follow-up, as "max_cens"): event_levels <- levels(new_data$event) rbind(   observed = prop.table(table(factor(observed_data$event, event_levels))),   simulated = prop.table(table(new_data$event)) ) #>           censoring cause1 cause2 max_cens #> observed      0.269  0.336  0.395    0.000 #> simulated     0.277  0.328  0.393    0.002
